title: Coalescence Dynamics of Two Unequal-Sized Compound Droplets
abstract: Abstract                   We comprehensively address the coalescence dynamics of two unequal-sized compound droplets suspended in a carrier fluid under the influence of a gravitational field. The deformation behavior of compound droplets, leading to the formation of satellite drops, is extensively analyzed under the influence of the core-to-shell droplet size, diameter ratio of parent drops, and viscosity of the droplets and surrounding fluid. The study identifies the relevant physicochemical parameters that dictate the pinch-off time, necking, partial coalescence, and complete coalescence, as well as the location of the pinch-off. The dynamic behaviors and the involved physical significance in the coalescence phenomena are separately presented for both shell and core-droplet coalescence. The study identifies two pinch-off stages: the first- and second-stage pinch-offs, which depend on the diameter ratio and viscosity of the fluids. The effect of propagating capillary waves generated at the droplets’ contact region along the interface diminishes for a minimal diameter ratio and hence delays the pinch-off. Also, the increasing viscous effect results in more drainage of the mother droplet, resulting in complete coalescence. Furthermore, the required diameter ratio to perceive partial coalescence at higher viscosity increases with an increase in the viscosity of the participating fluids.
